escalation_strategies.result: First-hand entry obtained (R9-F02a-P1). CAD reads aguhhu as 'an article of clothing, perhaps a sash', made of wool or leather, equated in the synonym list Malku II 230 with me-sir-ru, and worn after the Ur III period by Istar, by demons and once by Gilgames.

fresh_retrievals.source_citation: Breniquet, Catherine (2016). 'Que savons-nous exactement du kaunakes Mesopotamien ?', Revue d'assyriologie et d'archeologie orientale 110: 1-22; authorial abstract (French and English) as carried by a Cairn-derived archive record; the article's HAL record independently confirmed
fresh_retrievals.retrieval_method: FetchURL of the public archive record (abstract text rendered); HAL confirmation via the public HAL search API: curl 'https://api.archives-ouvertes.fr/search/?q=kaunakes&fl=title_s,uri_s,producedDate_s&wt=json' (numFound 1) and an author query returning the same record with files_s: 0
fresh_retrievals.source_locator: record 'Description' block, French abstract paragraphs 1 and 3, English abstract sentences 2-3; HAL record uca.hal.science/hal-01834706v1 (producedDate 2016, files: 0)
fresh_retrievals.source_excerpt: Depuis la decouverte des Sumeriens a Tello (Irak) en 1877, et les debats scientifiques suscites par leurs representations, les archeologues orientalistes ont pris l'habitude d'appeler 'kaunakes' un de leurs vetements qui apparait dans sa version minimale comme une sorte de jupe recouverte de meches. Toison d'animal pour certains, etoffe pour d'autres, on ne s'est jamais vraiment accorde sur la veritable nature de cette piece vestimentaire declinee en jupe, robe, voile et meme couverture, faute de decouverte archeologique non equivogue. | It remains unclear if this piece is an animal fleece or a true fabric, as no archaeological sample of this cloth was found. | (historiography) ... la joute scientifique qui a oppose Leon Heuzey, conservateur au Musee du Louvre a Paris, a Emile Cherblanc ... et leurs divergences de lecture des Guepes d'Aristophane qui contiendraient les cles de l'interpretation, en depit de l'anachronisme engendre par la date tres tardive de cet opus. | (programme) Un bilan sur les materiaux et techniques attestes en Mesopotamie dans la premiere moitie du IIIe millenaire avant J.-C.
fresh_retrievals.quote_fidelity_note: Accents and diacritics of the French/English abstract are rendered here without their accents because the JSON was authored in ASCII; wording, punctuation and sentence order are as retrieved. The archive record's own text is the publisher's abstract, not a third-party paraphrase.
fresh_retrievals.supports: First-hand authorial statement of the exact separation the entry's limit column requires: (i) the label is a modern (19th-century orientalist) habit of naming, (ii) the garment's true nature was never agreed (animal fleece vs fabric), (iii) no unequivocal archaeological sample was found, and (iv) the Greek key-text (Aristophanes' Wasps) is chronologically anachronistic for the Sumerian period. This supersedes round 8's second-hand mediation for these four propositions.
fresh_retrievals.support_scope: passage-level (publisher's abstract; the article body itself was not read)
fresh_retrievals.limits: Abstract-level only: the article's detailed arguments (historiography, textile-archaeology programme, material and technique inventory) remain unread; the abstract is the record's own machine-facing archive copy of the publisher's text.

fresh_retrievals.retrieval_method: curl -sSL of the HAL deposited PDF (HTTP 200, 718,471 bytes, application/pdf) piped to pdftotext -layout
fresh_retrievals.source_locator: introduction text: the paragraph on Mesopotamian textile remains and the Hallstatt comparison; the paragraph on bones/fleeces and iconography; the paragraph on Chalcolithic sheep varieties
fresh_retrievals.source_excerpt: Because of the poor state of the rare textile remains from Mesopotamia, the very well preserved Hallstatt sample of woolen textiles and fleeces represent a good case study. | As it is not possible to correlate directly bones and fleeces, iconography is integrated into the scientific approach as a mean of confirmation (E. Vila and D. Helmer). | It shows the existence of two sheep varieties in the Chalcolithic Near East - large sheep with spiral horns and a hairy coat, and small sheep with coiled horns and a woolly coat - which are both found on images. | (experimental session) It also made clear the different stages of cleaning and preparing wool for spinning, excluding the existence of carding for the period covered by the conference
fresh_retrievals.supports: First-hand methodological grounding for the entry's limit column: Mesopotamian textile remains are rare and poorly preserved; fleeces cannot be correlated directly with bones; iconography enters the method only as a means of confirmation. It also supplies the observable coat distinction (hairy vs woolly) that images can encode. This is the material-evidence reason why no 'actual fibre' answer for a specific third-millennium garment should be expected from imagery.
fresh_retrievals.limits: The volume introduction does not use the term kaunakes (grep count for 'kaunak' over the extracted text: 0, 2026-10-17) and is not about Early Dynastic garment construction specifically.

whole_claim_support.assessment: The row is supported, now on first-hand primary, scholarly and dated-object passages rather than round 8's mix of first-hand notices and second-hand scholarly quotations.
whole_claim_support.reasoning: (i) Primary/reference-work: the only native candidate term is read in CAD as a sash/belt, not a tufted skirt (P1), which supports both the row's non-commitment and the entry's decision not to adopt the Greek-derived label. (ii) Scholarly: the author whose article round 6 could not read states in her own abstract that the garment's nature was never agreed between animal fleece and fabric and that no unequivocal archaeological sample exists (P6); the open-access companion text states that Mesopotamian textile remains are rare/poorly preserved and that iconography serves at most as confirmation (P7). (iii) Dated objects: five Louvre notices (three new, P2-P4) describe dated Dynastic Archaic objects as wearing the garment type while making no fibre claim, and one record's wording ('dite kaunakes', 'meches laineuses') shows the institution itself separating the name from the material. (iv) Negative sweeps at the Met, Cleveland and Chicago (P8, P9) bound what other major collections' public records could add, and the failures list names exactly which routes stayed unreadable.
